app.name: CulitosTracker
app.tagline: Her cycle, your relationship, and how you're both doing. One place.

landing.intro: Track your partner's cycle with their consent, understand what phase they're in, keep the dates that matter and get suggestions based on how you're both doing.
landing.consent: Another person's data is stored only with their consent, and predictions are estimates: never a contraceptive method.

cycle.title: Cycle & phases
cycle.body: Menstruation, estimated fertile window and next date, computed from the real cycles you log.

relationship.title: The relationship
relationship.body: Anniversaries, milestones and time together, with advice that adapts to the stage you're in.

checkins.title: Check-ins from both
checkins.body: Each person logs how they feel. Nobody invents anybody's emotions.

ranking.title: A ranking for singles
ranking.body: An optional, anonymous leaderboard for those keeping count.

anniversary.today: Today is your anniversary: {{years}} years with {{name}}. Don't let it slip by, even something small counts.
anniversary.upcoming: Your anniversary is in {{days}} days ({{years}} years). Good moment to plan something special.
anniversary.approaching: Your anniversary is approaching ({{days}} days). If you want to organize something, now is the time.

partnerReport.sad: {{name}} said she's not feeling great today. You can ask if she wants to talk or just wants company.
partnerReport.low: {{name}} logged a rough day. Ask what she needs instead of assuming.

observation.needsSpace: You noted she seems to need some space. Consider asking her directly what she needs instead of assuming.
observation.sad: You noted she seems sad today. A simple message asking how she's doing can open the door without pressure.
observation.upset: You noted she seems upset. Listen first and understand what happened before defending or fixing.
observation.distant: You noted she seems distant. Sometimes it's tiredness, sometimes something else: ask without drama.

both.stressed: You both seem to be having a heavy day. Maybe today calls for something quiet rather than solving everything at once.
both.good: You both logged a good day. Take advantage: suggest that plan you keep postponing.

advice.quietPlan: You're tired and you've noticed stress in {{name}}. Maybe today is for a quiet plan and talking without pressure.

phase.menstruation: Based on the records, {{name}} might be on her period. Everyone experiences it differently: ask her what she feels like.

new.communication: Early on, asking beats assuming. Spend some time today learning something new about them.
new.boundaries: Talking about boundaries early avoids misunderstandings later. It doesn't have to be solemn.
new.expectations: Are you looking for the same thing? An honest conversation now saves confusion later.
new.consent: In intimacy, what works is asked, not guessed.

developing.deeper: You know each other now. Try a conversation beyond logistics: fears, plans, quirks.
developing.disagreements: The first disagreements set the tone. Arguing well takes practice too.
developing.newActivity: Try something neither of you has done: new plans build trust faster.
developing.routines: Knowing each other's routines (and respecting them) is a quiet way of caring.

established.routine: After a while together it's easy to fall into routine. Do one small thing today you don't usually do.
established.goals: Any shared plans for the future? Talking about them now and then keeps you on the same path.
established.details: Small details sustain more than grand gestures. One today, for no reason.
established.deepTalk: How long since you talked about how you are, not just logistics? Find a moment without screens.

longTerm.growth: Several years together: you've both changed. Ask what excites her now, you might be surprised.
longTerm.individuality: Protecting your own space also protects the relationship. A plan of your own this week isn't abandonment.
longTerm.newExperience: Against inertia, novelty: a new place, a different plan, even a small one.
longTerm.intimacy: Emotional intimacy also feeds on talking about the uncomfortable. No rush, but don't always avoid it.

veryLongTerm.memories: You have years of history. Revisiting a good memory together (photos, places) reconnects fast.
veryLongTerm.changes: Neither of you is the same person from years ago. Ask again about things you think you know.
veryLongTerm.projects: Any project you're both excited about? Shared plans renew long chapters.
veryLongTerm.curiosity: Mutual curiosity doesn't stay alive on its own, it's practiced. Today: a question you've never asked.

menstruation.comfort: Some people appreciate pampering, others prefer not to be touched. Ask what she feels like today.
menstruation.ask: Don't assume how she feels because of the phase: ask her. The calendar estimates dates, not emotions.

follicular.plan: If you want to plan something together, propose it early: choosing together is already part of the plan.
follicular.checkIn: A timely "how's your week going?" avoids a lot of misunderstandings.

ovulation.estimate: Remember: the ovulation shown is an estimate, not a certainty. Don't use it for contraception decisions.

luteal.patience: If one of you is having an off day, it doesn't always need fixing: sometimes company is enough.
luteal.selfCare: Taking care of yourselves separately also takes care of the relationship. Slowing down today is fine.

general.listen: Listening without composing your reply while the other talks: harder and more valuable than it seems.
general.smallGesture: A small gesture today (a message, her coffee, remembering something she said) beats a perfect plan someday.
general.time: Time together without screens is a different thing. Even twenty minutes.
general.gratitude: Saying out loud something you appreciate about each other changes the tone of the day. Try it.

xp.private: Your XP is private: it never appears in the ranking.

how.title: How it's calculated
how.base: Each encounter is worth a base 10 XP.
how.age: Partner's age: +1 XP per year over 18 (max +40).
how.weight: Recorded weight: +1 XP per 2 kg over 50 (max +25).
how.exclusive: Exclusive relationship (monogamous, engaged or married): everything ×1.5.
how.loyalty: Loyalty: +5% per consecutive encounter with the same person, up to +50%.
how.note: The multipliers stack: farming XP with a single person in a serious relationship yields up to ×2.25 per encounter.

privacy.title: Privacy & consent
privacy.intro: CulitosTracker stores sensitive information: menstrual cycles, emotions and relationship data. These are the rules it runs on.

consent.title: Consent
consent.body: When you register a person manually you confirm you have their consent to store their data, including cycle data. If that person creates their own account and links it, they decide what is shared back and can revoke it at any time.

checkins.title: Check-ins
checkins.body: Your check-ins are yours. The other person only sees your mood if you explicitly share it, and notes are never shared.

observations.title: Observations
observations.body: What you record about how your partner seems is your perception and only you see it. The app never presents it as a fact about the other person.

estimates.title: Cycle estimates
estimates.body: Phases, ovulation and the fertile window are estimates computed from the recorded data. They are not medical information and don't work as contraception.

leaderboard.title: Ranking
leaderboard.body: You only appear if you opt in. Only your alias, your emoji if you want, and an aggregate number are published. Never partner names, dates or notes.

authorization.title: Server-side authorization
authorization.body: Every request validates on the server that the data belongs to you or was shared with you. Hiding things in the interface is never the only barrier.

dates.datingAfterStart: The dating start date can't be after the relationship start.
dates.startAfterEngagement: The relationship start can't be after the engagement.
dates.engagementAfterMarriage: The engagement can't be after the marriage.
dates.datingAfterMarriage: Starting to date can't be after the marriage.
dates.endWithoutEnded: Only an ended relationship can have an end date.
dates.endBeforeStart: The end date can't be before the start.

period.futureStart: A period can't start in the future.
period.endBeforeStart: The period end can't be before its start.

checkIn.futureDate: You can't check in for a future date.

observation.futureDate: You can't record an observation for a future date.
